parent_note: The command as issued read ARCH-20260915-015-diagnosis; the advisor's own correction in the same message names ARCH-20260921-007, the 429-fix branch of record. Recorded as corrected.

distribution.note: Every 429 in every committed trace. Mined by joining each unit's failing `run` assertion to its header's model map and provider pins, and attributing the tier from the last node on the path.
distribution.time_window: 2026-09-20T02:09:33Z to 04:13:22Z — every event inside one 2h04m window
distribution.spend_killed: $0.2163 — the cost of the calls those twelve units paid for before the 429 ended them. Every dollar of it bought nothing.

characterisation: The exposure is concentrated absolutely, not merely mostly. **All 12 events are the same model — `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` — and all 12 are on the engineering tier**, spread across five different providers with no provider holding more than a quarter. The tier concentration is an artefact rather than a finding: engineering is the only tier that ran that model on those providers. **The control is decisive and sits in the same corpus: the triage tier runs the identical model via Alibaba across 309 committed units and has never once returned a 429.** So the axis is neither the model alone nor the provider alone but the (model, provider) pair, exactly as PR #15's live controls found. Within the window the events cluster by minute across providers — 03:10, 03:12, 03:16, 03:18 — which is consistent with a shortage moving through OpenRouter's upstream capacity rather than with any one host failing. The node split (implement 8, validate 3, domain_review 1) tracks call volume and payload size on the engineering tier and adds nothing causal.

post_fix.detail: The registered E1 run is the only paid run after PR #15 merged. Its log contains zero 429 lines, so **the retry never fired** — the shortage had cleared by then rather than being absorbed. The repair is therefore **untested in production**: it is proved only by `tests/test_rate_limit_retry.py`, five of whose eight tests fail against the unfixed client. Nothing in the committed record shows a retry succeeding against a real 429.
post_fix.consequence: The $0.2163 figure above is a pre-fix number and must not be presented as what the fix saves. What the fix would have done to those twelve units is unmeasured.

sufficient_for_pin_decisions: NO, and the reason is structural rather than a shortage of rows. Every event falls inside one 2-hour window on one day, so the sample describes an episode, not a rate. It cannot distinguish a provider that is usually short from one that was short that afternoon — and the serving ledger makes the point sharply: GMICloud carries 3 of these 12 events and also 227 completed units out of 236. A pin decision needs exposure measured across days, which no committed trace supplies.
what_the_free_record_cannot_answer: Whether the shortage was provider-side or OpenRouter-side. The body says 'rate-limited upstream' and the traces preserve no upstream identity beyond the provider name.
The base rate. Twelve events in one window with no denominator for the same window — the traces record failures, not attempts, so a 429-per-request rate cannot be computed.
Whether the retry would have rescued any of the twelve. Zero post-fix 429s means zero evidence either way.
Whether other models on the same providers were affected. Only `deepseek-v4-flash` ran on them in the corpus.

proposed_section_6_sentence.note: Offered for the advisor to rule on adopting; this command does not edit §6.
proposed_section_6_sentence.text: **A 429 is a property of the (model, provider) pair, not of the serving.** All twelve 429s in the committed record are `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, spread across five providers inside one two-hour window, while the same model via Alibaba ran 309 units without one. The pair plus `allow_fallbacks: False` is what converts a transient upstream shortage into a dead run; an unpinned rotation answered on demand throughout. Cost of the twelve: $0.2163, all of it buying nothing.
proposed_section_6_sentence.caveat_to_carry: One episode, one window, no denominator — sufficient to name the mechanism, not to rank servings.

acceptance_criteria_met.criterion: Distribution table with every 429 event accounted for, traced to its file.
acceptance_criteria_met.evidence: distribution.events — 12 of 12, each with its trace.

acceptance_criteria_met.criterion: Billed-retry cost quantified for post-fix events.
acceptance_criteria_met.evidence: Zero events, zero retries, $0.00 — and the consequence recorded: the repair is untested in production.

acceptance_criteria_met.criterion: An explicit statement of what the free record cannot answer.

questions_for_advisor: The finding that should change behaviour is not about any provider. It is that **$0.2163 of the session's $0.541 — two fifths — was spent by units that died on a condition the upstream itself calls transient and asks callers to retry.** The retry now exists but has never fired in production, so that fraction is what the repair is worth if the episode recurs, and nothing more is known.

Worth a ruling on whether `allow_fallbacks: False` should remain absolute. §6.1 justifies it as a quality control and the justification is sound — which serving answers decided two of this project's largest findings. But the same choice is what turns a two-hour upstream shortage into twelve dead runs. A middle position exists and is not currently expressible: pin for quality, permit fallback only after the bounded retries are exhausted, and record which serving actually answered. That is loop-adjacent configuration, so it is a ruling.
public_safe_summary: Free analysis, no spend. Twelve 429 events in the committed record, all on one model and all on the engineering tier, spread across five providers inside a single two-hour window — while the same model via Alibaba ran 309 units without one. The axis is the (model, provider) pair, confirming PR #15's live controls from the archive. The twelve units burned $0.2163 buying nothing. Zero post-fix events, so the retry repair has never fired in production and is proved only by its tests. The sample describes one episode rather than a rate and is explicitly insufficient for pin decisions.
